items.text: A Israeli airstrike reportedly kills a Palestinian medic at the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip. ((Reuters via The Times of Israel))
An Israeli airstrike reportedly kills senior brigadier general Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the head of the Hamas police force in the North Gaza Governorate, Gaza. ((Asharq Al-Awsat)) ((Reuters))

The Israeli military confirms that they have killed several Hamas militants over the past few weeks, including a Nukhba forces cell commander who took part in the Kissufim massacre during the October 7, 2023 attacks. ((The Times of Israel))
The naval forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims to have stopped four vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. ((Middle East Eye))

Iranian health ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reports no U.S. military strikes against Iran, after 13 consecutive nights of strikes by the U.S. Central Command against the country. ((NBC News))
The United States halts strikes against Iran after government officials reportedly saw a potential opening to resume diplomatic efforts and talks. ((Al-Monitor)) ((AP))

Two people are injured by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, Houthi-controlled Yemen. Saudi Arabia intercepts two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan. ((CNBC)) ((NBC News))
Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone strike on a postal facility in Sumy has killed two people. ((AFP via BGNES))

Darfur Joint Protection Force spokesperson Mutawakkil Ali Wakil confirms that, in coordination with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), that the joint force have retaken control of Umm Sayala, North Kordofan, Sudan, with 38 members of the Rapid Support Forces confirmed to have been killed. ((Sudan Horizon))

The SAF and Darfur Joint Protection Force recapture Jebrat al Sheikh alongside the North Kordofan towns of Bara and Al-Baraka. Additionally, Darfur governor Minni Arko Minawi confirms the recaptures. ((Sudan Tribune))
A fourth firefighter dies from injuries sustained in a wildfire at the Colorado–Utah border in the United States on June 27. ((The Guardian)) ((KUSA))
The death toll from the flash floods in Assam, India, rises to 62, after fourteen more fatalities are confirmed. ((NDTV))
At least 35 people are killed and 30 others are injured when two buses collide on the Deir ez-Zor–Damascus road in Syria. ((Reuters))
Two people are killed when a Tecnam P2010 aircraft crashes into a home in Ganderkesee, Lower Saxony, Germany. ((DPA via South China Morning Post))
One person is killed and at least 22 others are injured in a five-alarm fire in Flushing, New York City, United States. ((WNBC))

Brazil denies visas to two U.S. state department officials seeking election-related meetings in Brasília, citing risks of "political exploitation". The U.S. state department says the visit concerns electoral integrity and freedom of expression. ((AFP via Arab News))
A vehicle drives into a crowd at the pride festival in Berlin, Germany, killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run. ((CNN))

Brazil's Liberal Party formally nominates Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro's son, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming election. ((AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)) ((Reuters))

Indian education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns after protests over alleged entrance-examination leaks and broader education-system irregularities. His resignation marks the Modi government's first major concession to the demonstrations. ((AFP via Le Monde))

Two people are injured by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, Houthi-controlled Yemen. A Patriot battery operated by the Greek military intercepts two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan, Saudi Arabia. ((CNBC)) ((NBC News)) ((Al Jazeera))
Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old Lebanese-German, drives into a crowd at the pride festival in Berlin, Germany, killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run. ((CNN))

The Bishop of Aberdeen in Scotland declares the sedevacantist Sons of the Most Holy Redeemer religious institute, an order associated with the Society of Saint Pius X, to be excommunicated, after they consecrated a bishop without Vatican approval. ((The Herald)) ((The Catholic Herald))
